issues.legal_issue: A law that singles out particular persons in a private legal dispute, denies them judicial determination of their rights, and lacks a rational basis for distinguishing them from comparable persons violates the guarantee of equal protection.
material_facts: A public authority had settled land with the affected persons, who took possession and paid rent.
The legislature enacted a law declaring that particular settlement void and directing the affected persons’ eviction, without a judicial determination of the disputed rights.
Other persons held similar settlements, but their settlements were not subjected to the enactment.
The law deprived the affected persons of the ordinary opportunity to have the legality of the settlement and their rights determined by a court.
No rational classification or differentiating attribute was shown to justify singling out the affected persons.
issues.conclusion: The enactment was discriminatory and void for violating Article 14. The appeal was allowed, and a writ of mandamus was issued restraining action under the enactment and interference with the affected persons’ possession.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 permits legislative classification only when it is non-arbitrary and rests on a rational basis related to the legislative object. A law that singles out particular persons, imposes a disability not imposed on comparable persons, and removes their ability to obtain judicial determination of a private dispute is discriminatory. Although legislation is presumed constitutional, that presumption provides little or no assistance where the law contains no classification based on a differentiating attribute. Under Article 13, a law that abridges a fundamental right is void. The Court applied Ameerunnissa Begum v. Mahboob Begum and referred to Gulf of Colorado etc. Co. v. Ellis; it distinguished Chiran v. The Union of India.

rule.if: equal_protection_challenge and private_legal_dispute and law_targets_specific_parties and comparable_parties_not_targeted and judicial_determination_denied and not rational_classification

predicates.equal_protection_challenge: A person challenges a law on the ground that it denies equal protection.
predicates.private_legal_dispute: The law concerns a dispute between private parties over disputed legal rights.
predicates.law_targets_specific_parties: The law singles out particular persons or a particular transaction for a special legal disability.
predicates.comparable_parties_not_targeted: Other persons in materially similar circumstances are not subjected to the same legal disability.
predicates.judicial_determination_denied: The law prevents the affected persons from obtaining ordinary judicial determination of their disputed rights.
predicates.rational_classification: The law distinguishes the affected persons by a rational attribute related to its legislative object.

issues.definition: When an equal-protection challenge concerns a private dispute and a law targets specific parties, treats comparable parties differently, denies judicial determination, and has no rational classification, the targeted law is invalid and its enforcement is barred.
